scope: read-only public data probe for market-making sleeve (QTF-V08)

gap_analysis.missing_fill_conditioning: Recent-trade midpoint gives approximate fill price but not the exact limit-order fill level; adverse-selection requires knowing whether the fill was at bid, ask, or mid.
gap_analysis.missing_inventory_tracking: No historical order-placement/removal data from public API — cannot reconstruct inventory buildup from submitted but unfilled resting orders.
gap_analysis.missing_latency_data: REST polling introduces unknown latency between OB snapshot and fill; adverse-selection measurement requires sub-second timing.

gap_analysis.blocking_factor: Historical L2 order-book snapshots at sufficient frequency are not available from Bybit public REST API. The orderbook endpoint returns a point-in-time snapshot, not a time series. Without historical book evolution, we cannot track how resting inventory accumulates and decays.
gap_analysis.required_data: Time-series of L2 order-book states (at least every few seconds) with price, quantity, and update timestamps. This is only available via WebSocket replay (which requires subscription) or a purchased historical data feed.
gap_analysis.alternative_approach: Use tick-level trade data as a proxy for inventory changes (assuming trades come from market makers), but this conflates maker/taker flows and cannot distinguish between inventory accumulation and simple price discovery.

interpretation: Neither adverse-selection nor inventory-economics can be supported by public Bybit REST data alone. The market-making sleeve (QTF-V08) cannot proceed without historical L2 book time-series or WebSocket replay access.
next_unblocked_component: Obtain historical L2 order-book snapshots (WebSocket replay service or purchased data feed) to support inventory-economics analysis. Until then, the market-making sleeve remains blocked.
